summary:
Project Name
Mission Kitty-1 · Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

High-Level Project Summary
Mission Kitty-1 is a free, bilingual (English/Spanish) 3D voxel game for kids aged 7–12 that trains them as junior astronauts. Players train aboard a spaceship, land on Mars and run a small Mars base for 5 sols, deciding each morning how to share 4 sun-energy cubes between air, heat, food and an antenna to Earth. Each choice uses real NASA data: Curiosity’s radiation measurements, solar flares from NASA DONKI, the light-minutes of delay to Earth and making oxygen from water. Kids learn that space missions are about planning, trade-offs and science, not just rockets. It runs in any browser, even offline, with a teacher mode, a mission code for the whole class and a before/after mini-quiz.
details:
What it does: a complete mission in about 20–30 minutes. (1) An invitation letter at home. (2) A first-person spaceship with Commander Kitty and Luna, and 5 training missions; each one opens a “Vision 2” mini-game where the player becomes a water molecule, a radio signal, a sunray, a water shield or the landing spacecraft. (3) Landing on Mars and planting a flag. (4) Kitty Base: 5 sols of resource decisions with a shuffled event deck (dust storm, breakdown of the air machine, solar flare). (5) A diploma with the player’s decisions, radiation dose and what they learned.
How it works: every morning gives 4 sun cubes. Water is shared: each cube in the air machine uses 1 water to make air, and the same water is the shield against a solar flare. That makes the central trade-off “water to breathe or water for shielding”. Messages to Earth are answered the next day, which teaches communication delay. You can lose, with a clear explanation of what happened and a “what if” hint, and retry the day.
Every number is labelled REAL (measured by NASA), CALCULATED (worked out from NASA data) or SIMULATED (a game rule), and every REAL fact links to its source.
Benefits: it teaches systems thinking, energy, life support and space radiation at a child’s level. It is accessible: big-text and calm modes, an auto-walk “Luna, take me” button, touch and keyboard controls, voice narration and readable fonts.
Tools: vanilla JavaScript and three.js r128 in a single HTML file, with an offline build. Audio is made with WebAudio, without copyrighted music. It needs no installation, no account, and stores no personal data.
